holidays.name: National Freezer Pop Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate those plastic sleeves of sugary, brightly colored ice that stain your tongue and make summer bearable. Cut off the top, squeeze upward, and enjoy the brain freeze.
holidays.origin: Freezer pops were popularized by Fla-Vor-Ice in the 1950s and became a childhood staple. The date is an unofficial food observance tied to the height of summer heat.
holidays.funFact: Fla-Vor-Ice pops were so popular that the brand claimed to sell billions of pops, and many people swear the best flavor is the blue one, even though 'blue' isn't actually a fruit.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Day
holidays.description: A salute to the little blue orbs that star in muffins, pancakes, and pies. Celebrate by eating them straight from the carton, tossing them into smoothies, or baking something purple-tinged.
holidays.origin: Blueberry observances are tied to the July harvest in North America, where wild and cultivated blueberries peak during the summer months, and growers and food fans mark the occasion.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America, and Native peoples used them for food and medicine long before European settlers arrived.

holidays.name: Video Games Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day for gamers to put down their responsibilities and pick up controllers. Retro arcades, living room co-op sessions, and marathon quests are all encouraged.
holidays.origin: Gaming enthusiasts and fan communities adopted the date as an informal celebration of video games as an art form and a social hobby, with no formal government declaration behind it.
holidays.funFact: The first commercially sold arcade video game, Computer Space, appeared in 1971, and the industry has since grown larger than the movie and music industries in revenue by many estimates.

holidays.name: Math 2.0 Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating new, creative, and collaborative ways of learning and using mathematics, inspired by making math less scary and more social, tech-savvy, and fun.
holidays.origin: Math 2.0 Day was created by a math education advocate to promote the idea of 'Math 2.0', where technology and online communities are used to learn and share mathematical thinking.
holidays.funFact: The equals sign was invented in 1557 by Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde, who chose two parallel lines because 'no two things can be more equal.'

holidays.name: Be Nice to Your Eyes Day
holidays.description: Give your peepers a break from screens, glare, and squinting. It's a day to rest your eyes, get a checkup, and wear sunglasses without feeling like a spy.
holidays.origin: A health-minded unofficial observance meant to encourage eye care during summer, when UV exposure from the sun is at its peak and people spend long hours outdoors or on screens.
holidays.funFact: The 20-20-20 rule recommends that every 20 minutes you look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds to reduce digital eye strain.
